Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders. Ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you succeed and get the most out of your experience. About Mars, Incorporated For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. This idea is at the center of who we have always been as a global, family-owned business. Today, Mars is transforming, innovating, and evolving in ways that affirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the world around us. Across our diverse and expanding portfolio of Snacking, Food, and Petcare products and services, we employ over 140,000 dedicated Associates who are all moving in the same direction: forward. As a $65 billion family-owned business, we produce some of the world’s best-loved brands including ROYAL CANIN®, PEDIGREE®, WHISKAS®, CESAR®, M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, Pringles®, Cheez-It®, and BEN’S ORIGINAL™. and take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health and services businesses, including AniCura, Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, and VCA™. We know we can only be truly successful if our partners and the communities in which we operate prosper as well. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today.

jobs.description: Employer: S. W. Cole Engineering, Inc. Expires: 11/19/2026 We are currently accepting applications for an Internship to be based at our office in Londonderry, New Hampshire during the summer of 2027 for current students in a 2 or 4 year program in civil, geotechnical, or structural engineering, construction management or related field. The selected candidate will work as a Construction Services Field and Laboratory Technician. To learn more about what you can expect, check out our Intern page of our web site at https://swcole.com/inside-the-s-w-cole-intern-experience/ and hear from some of our prior Interns through a video about their experience. This position involves field and laboratory testing of construction materials (soil, concrete, grout, masonry, asphalt, aggregate and other materials) associated with a variety of construction projects. Interns will have the opportunity to learn how to read and interpret construction specifications and plans, and to obtain related certifications for construction materials testing of concrete and soil. We anticipate the job will require working up to 40 hours or more per week during the summer months with the potential for part time work or a co-op in the Fall of 2027. Interns will also have the opportunity to work with our Geotechnical Engineering team conducting subsurface investigations with exploration drilling crews. S. W. Cole Engineering is an established employee owned firm with a history of over 45 years of success and stable growth serving clients throughout New England. Job RequirementsCandidates must be able to follow verbal and written instructions to complete laboratory and field tests, have a general understanding of computers and ability to learn and use new software programs, and have the ability to read and learn to interpret construction specifications and plans. Familiarity with construction and/or engineering concepts is preferred, but not required. The physical and mental requirements for this position include lifting up to 75 pounds frequently, as well as moving heavier loads (such as 5-gallon buckets containing soil), stand for long periods of time, as well as move up and down from kneeling to crouching to bending. Must learn to properly operate company equipment, be able to properly transport samples and equipment over uneven ground with varying conditions (including tripping hazards, ice and snow, brush, construction staging, etc.). Requires close, distance, and peripheral vision. Ability to interact appropriately with a variety of individuals including but not limited to coworkers, supervisors, clients. Ability to remember and understand verbal and written instructions including laboratory test procedures. Ability to reason logically and make decisions. The Intern is occasionally exposed to variable and potentially extreme weather and temperature conditions. Applicants must have good verbal and written communication skills: Will be required to effectively communicate verbally to clients, project team members, supervisors and coworkers. Will be required to write effectively to take notes, record observations and data, and write emails and text messages on a daily basis. Candidates must be able to apply basic math skills for compiling and calculating data. Applicants must have reliable transportation, a valid driver’s license, active automobile insurance and an acceptable driving record. jobs.description: Employer: Southeast Conservation Corps Expires: 11/19/2026 AmeriCorps Individual Placement – Engineering TechnicianOrganization: Southeast Conservation Corps, a program of Conservation LegacySite Location: Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, Blue Ridge Ranger District2042 Highway 515 WBlairsville, GA 30512Term of Service: 50 weeksStart Date: 04/05/2027End Date: 03/17/2028AmeriCorps Slot Classification: 1700 hrStatus: This is a full-time, seasonal, 50-week, 1700-hour AmeriCorps National Service Program.Benefits:Segal AmeriCorps Education Award of $7,395.00 upon successful completion of the programLiving allowance of $480.00 per week, paid bi-weeklyAdditional Benefit of $465.00 per week, paid bi-weeklyAmeriCorps health insurance, uniform shirts, personal protective equipment, Public Land Corps Hiring Authority Certificate (upon successful completion of hours), member assistance program, and other professional development opportunities availablePositions Available: 1PurposeSoutheast Conservation Corps (SECC): Empowering youth and adults to cultivate compassion, responsibility and life skills through community service, hard work and land stewardship.Southeast Conservation Corps, a program of Conservation Legacy, is a non-profit AmeriCorps program. We engage youth (age 15-17) and young adults (ages 18-30, up to 35 for veterans) in service projects on public lands throughout the Southeast. SECC collaborates with land management agencies (United States Forest Service, National Park Service, State Parks, local municipalities, and non-profits) to host day or overnight camping crews and individual placements.Our AmeriCorps positions provide impactful educational and service opportunities that benefit both communities and landscapes. SECC's participants reflect the population of the Southeast region, including youth, graduates, veterans, and individuals from various backgrounds.United States Forest Service: The phrase "Caring for the Land and Serving People," captures the Forest Service mission. As set forth in law, the mission is to achieve quality land management under the sustainable multiple-use management concept to meet the many needs of people.Blue Ridge Ranger District: The Blue Ridge Ranger District Civil Engineering Program is responsible for approximately 500 miles of Forest Service roads within the district's area of responsibility. Duties include data collection, survey, maintenance, repair, and inspection of roadways ranging from suitable passenger cars to high clearance vehicle-only roads. Additionally, Civil Engineering duties include data collection, inspection, survey, and limited scope maintenance and repair of Forest Service facilities.Position Overview:This Individual Placement is designed to provide an entry-level professional opportunity to serve directly with a federal land management agency, developing relevant skills, qualifications, and experience. The projects will focus on field data collection to provide a comprehensive assessment of current conditions in relation to recent natural disasters and weather impacts. Hurricane Helene, along with many other recent impacts, has created significant impacts on the Blue Ridge Ranger District.The Individual Placement will serve alongside Forest Service technicians and specialists in various resource areas, including trail management, wilderness stewardship, engineering, archaeology, outdoor recreational facilities, wildlife management, silviculture, forestry, and wildland fire management. Most tasks will be primarily focused on erosion control. Storm-damaged or improperly maintained roads lead to erosion, resulting in excessive entry of pollutants into waterways. Out of the district's 500 miles of road, it is estimated to seek improvements of approximately 150 to 200 miles during this period of disaster repair.While the service project will focus on road engineering related tasks, utilizing GIS technology and associated devices to collect real-time data from the field, the exposure and training are designed to provide the Individual Placement with the experience necessary to compete for an entry-level position with a land management agency upon program completion.Description of Duties:Roadway Disaster Data CollectionServe with the Supervisor to gain an understanding of the data needed and the overall intent of the assessment.Build an assessment plan for the district to prioritize different resource needs and concerns.Gain proficiency with GIS technology and applicationsKeep consistent records of data gathered.Maintenance PlanningServe with the Engineering Technician to gain an understanding of road condition expectations.Assist Engineering with routine activities to include road condition surveys, site assessments, mapping, road feature counts, etc...Assist in Engineering to prioritize needs.Assist Engineering in plan development, 811 marking, cost estimate, and procurement.Maintenance OperationsAssist Engineering with safety notifications, site preparation, and pre-stage.Assist Engineering with mobilization.Use a variety of hand tools, power tools, and limited complexity equipment operation under the supervision of certified personnel.Assist team with clean-up and monitoring after the day is completed.Potential environmental/human risk involved with this term of service: uneven terrain, physical exertion, inclement weather, and remote service sites.Qualifications:United States citizen, United States national, or a lawful permanent resident alienMust be between the ages of 18 and 30, or up to 35 if a military veteran.Has received a high school diploma or equivalency certificate; or has not dropped out of elementary or secondary school to enroll as an AmeriCorps participant, and agrees to obtain a high school diploma or its equivalent before using the education awardAgrees to provide information to establish eligibility and to complete a National Service Criminal History CheckExcellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.Strong interest in road construction, serving outdoors, and natural resource management.Proven ability to complete assignments and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.Comfortable navigating by map throughout the forest, including areas with limited or no cell coverage.You must possess a valid driver's license and pass Conservation Legacy's Driver Insurability requirements.Preferred Qualifications:Experience with hand tools, power tools, and tractors.Crosscut or chainsaw sawyer Certification.Experience with navigation by map and terrain association.Experience with ESRI Field Maps, Survey123, and ArcGIS software.Transportation:A personal vehicle is required to report to/from the service site/office, and for all personal business. A USFS/SECC vehicle will be provided for transportation to conduct operations within the forest. This Individual Placement must be a driver and pass Conservation Legacy's driver insurability requirements.Housing:Housing will not be provided. USFS staff will assist with finding housing in the local area near the park.Physical Requirements:Conservation Legacy is committed to the full consideration of all qualified individuals and will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to perform essential functions. Some positions may require periodic overnight travel, non-traditional hours, ability to move across varied terrain, use program-specific tools and a range of technology on an infrequent or frequent basis. Exerting up to 25 pounds of force occasionally to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects. Ability to safely drive an organizational vehicle may also be required for some positions. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during application or recruiting process, please send a request to the hiring manager.Time Requirements:Typically, this position is expected to serve from 8 am – 5pm, Monday through Friday, 40 hours per week – but exact service schedules may vary and will include evening and weekend service depending on project needs.A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service.Members may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term.Orientation and Training:Members will receive an orientation that includes training on AmeriCorps prohibited and unallowable activities.Defensive Driving – how to drive on gravel/USFS roadsArcGIS, Survey123, FieldMaps, Avenza, USDA Guidelines for Maintenance LevelsEvaluation and Reporting:As an AmeriCorps member, performance will be evaluated on whether the member has completed the required number of hours, the member has satisfactorily completed assignments, and if the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service.Reporting requirements include, but are not limited to:Bi-weekly timesheetsMonthly Accomplishment ReportNarrative Monthly ReportBi-Monthly Check-InsMidterm and Final EvalsExiting TasksSubstance Free:In accordance with a drug-free environment, alcohol and drugs are prohibited while participating in AmeriCorps and program activities and while on organization property.Contact questions about the application process, please contact:Angela GerstnerIndividual Placements CoordinatorSoutheast Conservation Corpsagerstner@conservationlegacy.orgEqual Opportunity NXP brings together secure edge intelligence, advanced semiconductor solutions, and deep system expertise to help customers build what’s next. Our Global Sales and Applications organization partners with customers to align technical solutions to application requirements, solve integration challenges, and accelerate design wins. We are seeking a technically curious engineering student to join our Field Applications team and help enable the integration of NXP semiconductor technologies into real customer systems.Program OverviewThe NXP Americas Global Sales & Applications Summer Internship is a 12 week, paid program for rising juniors, seniors, and graduate students who combine a strong technical foundation with the drive and curiosity to work directly with customers. Interns are embedded in the Field Application Engineering organization, paired with an experienced FAE mentor, and assigned meaningful technical work from day one.This internship is a primary pipeline into NXP’s Technical Sales & Applications Program (TSAP), our early-career pathway for full-time technical sales and applications roles. Strong performers may receive a return offer upon graduation. What You'll DoAs a Field Applications Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced FAEs on customer-facing technical projects with real business impact. You will help translate application requirements into practical NXP-based solutions, support evaluations and proof-of-concepts, and develop hands-on experience with embedded systems, lab validation, and design-in activity. configure SDKs and development environments; and integrate example software into application prototypes.Develop or modify firmware and application code in C, C++, Python, or similar languages under the guidance of experienced engineers.Support embedded software debugging and system integration across real-time control, sensor interfaces, connectivity, Linux, or RTOS-based applications.Lab Validation & Design SupportPerform product evaluation, lab validation, and basic system-level troubleshooting using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, power supplies, current/voltage probes, power analyzers, and software debug or trace tools.Assist with schematic and PCB reviews, interface checks, power-up sequencing, signal observations, and hardware/software integration investigations.Create concise test plans, capture measurements, organize results, and communicate conclusions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.Technical Enablement & CommunicationPrepare customer-ready technical presentations, demonstrations, quick-start guides, application notes, and training material with guidance from senior engineers.Capture customer feedback and collaborate with sales, marketing, product management, product-line, and engineering teams to improve tools, software, documentation, and support content.Present your summer project findings, technical approach, results, and recommendations to sales and applications leadership in a final intern capstone presentation. About YouMinimum QualificationsCurrently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.Rising junior, senior, or graduate student — expected graduation between December 2027 and June 2029.Cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0 or higher.Authorization to work in the United States (no sponsorship available for intern roles).Availability for 12 weeks full-time during Summer 2027 (May–August).Preferred QualificationsCoursework or project experience in embedded systems, analog and digital circuits, computer architecture, microcontrollers/processors, wireless communications, power electronics, control systems, or semiconductor applications.Hands-on experience with microcontrollers, MPUs, FPGAs, development boards, evaluation kits, or reference designs; familiarity with ARM-based systems is a plus.Programming experience in C, C++, Python, or similar languages, with exposure to IDEs, SDKs, version control, RTOS basics, or embedded Linux.Familiarity with common embedded interfaces such as UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, USB, or Ethernet.Experience using or willingness to learn common lab equipment, schematic/PCB review, board bring-up, firmware debugging, sensor integration, motor control, edge AI, or robotics applications.Who Thrives HereYou are curious about how semiconductor products solve real-world system problems and enjoy learning by building and testing.You approach debugging methodically: form a hypothesis, measure the system, isolate variables, and document the result.You communicate clearly with engineers, customers, sales teams, and non-technical stakeholders.You are proactive, take ownership, collaborate well, and adapt to changing priorities in a customer-focused environment.You are motivated to develop both technical expertise and business understanding while contributing to team results.What You'll GetCompetitive paid hourly compensation.Dedicated FAE/TSE mentor and day-to-day manager support throughout the program.Hands-on exposure to the semiconductor applications cycle—from requirements discovery and technical evaluation through proof-of-concept and design-in support.Participation in intern cohort events, including professional development workshops, executive speaker sessions, and cross-functional networking opportunities.Access to structured learning on NXP product portfolios, embedded systems, customer applications, and the semiconductor industry.Potential relocation support or housing stipend (location-dependent).Consideration for a return full-time offer into NXP's TSAP program upon graduation.LocationsField Sales Offices across the United States — including but not limited to: Austin, TX | Detroit, MI | San Jose, CAPreferred location will be discussed during the interview process. The visual requirements include demonstrating or having vision corrected to 20/20. In general, this position includes sedentary work that primarily involves sitting and/or standing as well as repeating motions that include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.

This means you approach your work with a growth mindset and find ways to leverage AI to help make faster, smarter decisions that will 10X your impact at Box.Education & Placement Requirement: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree requiring a recognized 12-month industrial sandwich placement year before your final year of study (open to all academic disciplines; Business, Management, or Marketing is a plus, but not required).Growth Mindset & Curiosity: Demonstrates resilience, high energy, a proactive "can-do" attitude, and an eager appetite to learn about enterprise SaaS, cloud software, and AI technologies.Strong Communication & Interpersonal Presence: Articulate verbal and written communication skills with the confidence to build professional relationships with senior stakeholders across multiple channels.Commercial Acumen & Problem Solving: Analytical mindset with the ability to identify business trends, creatively uncover growth opportunities, and connect customer challenges to digital solutions.Organization & Detail Orientation: Strong time management skills, comfort prioritizing tasks in a fast-paced environment, and the ability to maintain high data quality and accuracy.Languages: Fluent German or French is an advantage but not requiredBox lives its values, with community and in-person collaboration being a core part of our culture. jobs.title: Traditional Trades Advancement Program - Stones River National Battlefield at American Conservation Experience
jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 11/21/2026 SummaryAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with the National Park Service, is seeking TWO members to contribute to historic preservation projects alongside Stones River National Battlefield staff.The Traditional Trades Advancement Program is intended for enthusiastic individuals who want to gain experience in the fields of historic preservation and horticulture. No education or experience in the field is necessary.For more information about ACE, please visit our website.Start Date: 01/04/2027Estimated End Date: 07/03/2027*a 26-week minimum commitment is required *Location Details/Description: Located in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, Stones River National Battlefield is made up of over 600 acres of living landscape that has been shaped by environmental factors throughout history. The Stones River is just one of many natural features in the park, including native grasslands, forests, karst topography, and rare limestone cedar glades. The park is also home to many plants, animals, fungi, and other living things, providing essential habitat in a growing urban area. Natural resource management plays an important part in preserving the natural history of the battlefield.For more information about Stones River National Battlefield, please visit the NPS website.Position Overview: Interns will assist in general seasonal maintenance of specimen trees in the historic cemetery. Pruning is a recurring activity during the winter and interns will learn about the process while having the opportunity to assist with pruning from aerial platforms and learning basic tree rigging on the ground. Tree root health maintenance is a primary focus this coming winter and interns will assist with establishing mulch rings around trees and aerating the root zone using compressed air excavators. Along with hands-on training interns will also be presented with theory of various pruning cuts/strategies, learning to tie knots, equipment inspection, and tree identification. Other activities may include headstone cleaning, tree lightening protection installation, tree cabling, and assisting other divisions.The knowledge and skills gained by interns will be directly transferable to entry-level qualifications similar to what might be expected for an NPS WG-5 Maintenance Worker position. The work projects are representative of recurring maintenance needs found on cultural landscapes of which there will continue to be an ongoing need for experienced laborers. We will also provide opportunities for interns to collaborate with the interpretive division on additional projects to broaden the experiences they are exposed to.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. This could include gaining experience in different conservation fields and shadowing different work groups.Schedule: Biweekly schedule (alternates every week)Week 1 Schedule: Monday through Friday (6:30am - 4:00pm) Week 2 Schedule: Monday through Wednesday (6:30am - 4:00pm), Thursday (6:30am - 3:00pm), Friday (Off Day)Position BenefitsLiving Allowance: The ACE Member is expected to contribute ~40 hours/week and will receive a living allowance of $800/week to offset the costs of food and incidental expenses, dispersed bi-weekly.This position is part of the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority: Members serving under this agreement must meet the PLC Eligibility requirements to be considered for this position. Members may be eligible for a federal hiring authority upon completion of their term of service and 640 hours of service. If the duration of a PLC-eligible term is not long enough for Members to accrue 640 hours of service (~16 weeks), the total hours served at the completion of the term may be eligible to be combined with hours accrued from another PLC-eligible term to meet the 640 hours requirement. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age (You must be between the ages of 16 and 30. Some agencies also interpret these guidelines to include veterans up to age 35) and citizenship. Please contact ACE staff with questions about eligibility, or view general eligibility information on our website.Housing: NPS Housing may be available at a cost but is not guaranteed. Housing is the responsibility of the member and not guaranteed to be provided by ACE or NPSProvided Training/Orientation: ACE members will receive position specific training and an orientation outlining ACE policies and procedures, clear guidance on prohibited activities, and networks for support. Interns will also participate in National Park Service Operational Leadership training. This training will provide interns with the knowledge necessary to communicate health and safety concerns with their coworkers, leaders, and supervisors. Prior to engaging in any new activity, interns will receive hands-on demonstration of tools, equipment, and techniques from experienced workers. STRI will provide personal protective equipment and will communicate additional individual needs with interns as necessary. STRI will provide basic first aid and CPR training. Qualifications Required:Members must be authorized to work in the United States. ACE does not provide sponsorship for employment visas. Willing and able to represent ACE and the partner organization in a professional, positive, and enthusiastic manner. Ability to be both self-directed/work alone, and be a positive, contributing member of a group.Members will be required to operate off-highway UTVs. Training for UTV’s will be necessary and provided. A valid driver's license and an insurable driving record (documentation to be provided upon request). Members must be 21+ to drive due to ACE’s insurance and liability requirements.A current and valid form of ID (will be required to provide copies of ID’s upon hiring)Willing to undergo and must pass the required criminal history checks Ability to perform the essential duties of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.ACE Members will need to complete bi-weekly timesheets, beginning of term feedback forms, end of term evaluations and for longer terms, a mid-term evaluation. Members may not participate in any prohibited activities as listed in the Member Service Agreement.To learn more about eligibility requirements, please visit our website.Preferred:Competitive applicants for this position can hold or be pursuing a minimum of a high school diploma or GED.Ability and willingness to take directions and participate in a team. Desire and ability both to engage in the work and to establish themselves in the trade fieldDeep interest in historic and landscape preservation.Physical Demands, Work Environment and Working Conditions:Physical Demands: May be physically demanding. Requires frequent sitting, standing, walking, carrying, using hands to handle or feel, reaching with hands and arms, talking and hearing. Manual dexterity required for [use of various tools, computer keyboard/mouse and other office equipment. Required to stoop, kneel, climb stairs, and/or crouch. Requires fine motor skills for tying knots. Ability to perform work with minimal breaks for up to 8 hours per day.Vision Requirements: Requires close, distance, peripheral and depth perception vision as well as the ability to focus. Weight Lifted or Force Exerted: Frequently moves up to 25 lbs., ability to move up to 50 pounds.Environmental: Outdoor and indoor conditions. Work environment conditions can change frequently and may include the following: freezing temperature, hot and/or humid conditions (heat Index up to approx. 110 degrees, rain, wind, snow, insects, dust.Noise Environment: Moderate to high noise such as gas-powered chainsaws and other hand and power tools, and tractors/utv/similar equipment.Travel: This position does not require unique travel. Environmental Conditions/Hazards: The ACE member(s) may encounter environmental conditions/hazards including extreme heat or cold, rocky terrain, swamp or wetland conditions, biting insects, and potentially dangerous wildlife. The member is expected to conduct duties in a safe and orderly manner so as not to endanger self, fellow staff/members or resources. Unique hazards may include working at heights, overhead falling objects, and ropes under tension. Vehicle and Equipment Use/Safety: If a vehicle is required for the accomplishment of the duties, one will be provided by the NPS or ACE. Any tools required for the accomplishment of the duties will be provided by the NPS. Use of personal protective equipment (PPE), typically provided by the NPS, will be mandatory for any activity that requires it. Strict adherence to NPS and ACE equipment training, certification and safety protocols is required. To Apply: Please submit your resume, a cover letter demonstrating your interest and experience, and contact information for three professional/academic references to ACE’s online application page for this position on our website.Early consideration will be given as applications are received. This position may close at any time. If you have any questions regarding this position please feel free to contact ACE EPIC NPS Senior Member Manager, Sabrina Caruso.If you meet at least 70 percent of the qualifications, we want to hear from you!ACE participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information when you are enrolled in a program to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.EEO: Employment or Service with ACE is based upon ability, qualifications, attitude, and job-related factors. Every qualified employee, member, or applicant has the same opportunity for recruitment, hire, training, transfer, promotion, compensation, demotion, termination, benefits, employee activities, and general treatment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, creed, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran or military status, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, medical condition, marital or parental status, political affiliation, ethnicity, hair texture or style, arrest record, caste, hereditary status, endogamy, or any other classification protected by applicable local, state, or federal law.

jobs.description: Employer: Stefanini Expires: 11/21/2026 Stefanini Group is hiring!Stefanini is looking for Desktop Support Apprentice in Dover, DE For quick Apply, please reach out to Rachit Rastogi - call: 2489360662/ email: rachit.rastogi@stefanini.comWork Hours: M-F (37 hours)Work Location: Dover, DE Shift: 1st Shift – 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM The DTI(Department of Technology and Information) Technology Apprentice Program (TAP) aims to provide training and experience to prepare participants for future career opportunities in state government IT positions. The Technology Apprentice role is an entry-level position designed to provide hands-on learning and professional development in information technology. This role combines practical work experience with structured training to build foundational skills and enhance knowledge in providing IT support services to state government agencies. Work Environment:This position is based on site at DTI office locations in Dover, DE. Remote work may be considered for up to one (1) day per week once the apprentice has shown the ability to complete work independently. Remote work is not guaranteed and is at the discretion of the apprentice's direct supervisor and the DTI Program Lead. Some positions are not suited to remote work, and apprentices in those positions are expected to work on site 100% of the time for the full program.DTI's office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding State holidays. Apprentices work up to 37.5 hours per week, and the program runs program runs for 6 months from start. Apprentices will not be assigned after-hours, shift, or on-call work.The role typically involves working in an office setting, potentially with occasional travel to other state facilities and may require lifting and moving computer equipment up to 50 pounds. Longroad has developed or acquired 7.6 GW of renewable energy projects and has raised $20.6 billion of equity, debt, and tax equity to support completion of its portfolio. Today, Longroad owns 5.8 GW of wind, solar, and storage projects and operates and manages a total of 7.4 GW on behalf of Longroad and third parties. Longroad is owned by the Infratil Limited, NZ Superannuation Fund, Longroad Energy Partners, LLC, and MEAG MUNICH ERGO Asset Management. Program DescriptionLongroad Energy’s internship program provides opportunities for undergraduate students to explore careers in renewable energy. In 2027, Longroad will offer paid internship positions that create challenging hands-on learning experiences for college juniors, entering their senior year in the Fall. Selected interns will participate in a 10–12-week summer program that includes onboarding, structured work experience, mentoring, and exposure both to department-specific and company-wide personnel and activities. Job PurposeThe Transmission Intern will support the identification and evaluation of optimal locations for new renewable energy projects within the transmission grid. By assisting with transmission prospecting, data analysis, and the use of specialized tools, the intern will contribute to expanding the company’s project pipeline. This role provides hands-on experience in power systems and renewable project development while supporting the team’s strategic growth objectives. This role is hybrid, based out of our Boston office. Responsibilities & Tasks:Assist with transmission prospecting by analyzing grid maps, system data, and available capacity.Use tools such as TARA, PSSE, Google Earth, and Landgate to evaluate potential project locations.Compile and organize transmission and land data to support development decisions.Conduct research on transmission planning studies, queue positions, and system upgrades.Prepare summaries, maps, and visuals to communicate findings to the development teamParticipate in team meetings and present progress on assigned tasks.Document methodologies and results to ensure knowledge transfer and repeatability.Qualifications:Undergraduate student at a 4-year collegePreferred major of Electrical EngineeringCourse work in power systems (e.g., power system analysis, electrical machines, power electronics, renewable energy systems, energy markets & policy)GPA of 3.0 or higherInterest in Renewable Energy IndustryCuriositySelf-starterStrong written and organizational skillsMicrosoft Excel proficiencyCover letter highly preferredCompensation:This role pays $25 hour. OtherApplicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. The Company does not sponsor applicants for work visas. Benefits of Working at Longroad Energy We are dedicated to providing our employees with the support and resources they need to stay healthy, secure their future, and be successful in their careers. Benefits at Longroad include the opportunity for merit-based salary increases, incentive plan participation, eligibility for our 401 (k) plan and matching, and comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Our robust time-off policy includes accrual of 18 vacation days in your first year, paid holidays, and paid volunteer time. We offer paid parental leave to help support employees as they transition into parenthood. Learn more about our employee benefits. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Diversity, equity, and inclusion matter - at Longroad, in our industry, in our communities, and in society at large. We embrace our responsibility to build and promote a diverse, equitable, and inclusive working experience and drive change where we live and operate. We work to actively promote and celebrate diversity, equity, and inclusion. We foster a supportive space that empowers everyone at Longroad to learn about, discuss and ask questions related to embracing and honoring identity. We collaborate with our community, colleagues, and industry in the ongoing pursuit of evolving and growing an inclusive and diverse environment. Learn more about our DEI commitment. Longroad Energy Values At Longroad, we SHINE. We aim to be the most trusted renewable energy company on the long road to a green future. We are an experienced team of problem solvers and promise-keepers who develop sustainable solutions that meet today’s challenges and make a lasting impact on people and our planet. Learn more about our SHINE values. Longroad Energy is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer (“EOE”). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, citizenship, or any other legally protected status. Longroad Energy prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities and will reasonably accommodate applicants with a disability, upon request, and will also ensure reasonable accommodations are made for disabled employees. Longroad Energy is firmly committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities in all employment practices and personnel actions, including advertising, recruitment, testing, screening, hiring, selection for training, upgrading, transfer, demotion, layoff, discipline, termination, rates of pay, and other forms of compensation.Notice of AI Use in Job Application ReviewAs part of our commitment in creating a fair, efficient, and consistent hiring process we may use artificial intelligence (AI) to help our recruiting teams organize, summarize, and analyze information provided by candidates, including resumes, application responses, and other materials submitted during the application process.AI may be used to identify patterns, highlight relevant skills, and experience, and assist in comparing a candidate’s qualifications with the requirement of a specific role. These tools are to improve efficiency and consistency while supporting more informed hiring decisions, which will ultimately be made by the hiring team.

jobs.description: Employer: CHS Inc. Expires: 11/22/2026 SummaryCHS has an exciting opportunity within the Building & Office Services department for a summer Corporate Landscape & Grounds Management Intern. The Corporate Campus Landscape & Grounds Management Internship is part of the CHS Summer Internship Program and provides exposure to corporate facilities management, landscape architecture, arboriculture, horticulture, sustainability, campus planning, and grounds operations. Interns will gain hands-on experience while contributing to projects that enhance the employee experience and environmental stewardship of the CHS Corporate Campus. This intern will serve as a valued member of the Building & Office Services team, contributing to and/or leading a variety of projects supported across the team, such as landscape design, project management, invasive species mitigation, tree care, vendor management, and more. You must be detail-oriented, independent, and eager to learn with excellent communications skills and the ability to handle multiple projects concurrently. To maximize the internship experience, this position will follow an on-site structure, spending 5 days each week on campus based at CHS in Inver Grove Heights, MN.ResponsibilitiesAssist in the maintenance and enhancement of the 30-acre CHS Corporate Campus landscape, including turfgrass, trees, planting beds, native landscapes, and outdoor gathering spaces.Support landscape architecture and grounds improvement projects from planning through implementation. Participate in campus beautification initiatives, seasonal color displays, and landscape renovation projects. Conduct tree inventories, assessments, and support arboriculture programs focused on tree health, preservation, and replacement planning.Assist with invasive species identification, monitoring, mitigation, and ecological restoration efforts.Support turfgrass management activities including mowing evaluations, fertilization planning, irrigation monitoring, and integrated pest management practices.Collaborate with vendors and contractors to monitor project progress, quality standards, and safety requirements. Assist with development and maintenance of campus landscape maps, asset inventories, and project documentation.Participate in sustainability initiatives related to pollinator habitats, native plantings, water conservation, and environmental stewardship.Conduct site inspections and provide recommendations for improving campus appearance, functionality, and user experience.Support project budgeting, bid review processes, vendor coordination, and project management activities.Assist with campus event preparations, including outdoor venue setup and coordination.Utilize technology and software tools to track projects, document findings, and communicate recommendations.Partner with Building & Office Services team members on facilities, safety, and operational improvement initiatives.Present project updates, findings, and recommendations to department leadership upon completion of assigned projects.Minimum Qualifications (required)Currently pursuing a bachelor's or associate degree in Landscape Architecture, Arboriculture, Horticulture, Turfgrass Management, Grounds Management, Natural Resources, Environmental Science, Facilities Management, or a related field.Valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record; ability to operate company vehicles and on-site utility/ATV equipment for occasional groundskeeping and facility-support tasks.Additional QualificationsRising sophomore, junior, senior, or graduate student with anticipated enrollment following the internship.Strong interest in landscape management, grounds operations, environmental stewardship, or corporate campus planning, with a passion for creating and maintaining attractive, safe, functional, and sustainable outdoor environments.Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions and perform site inspections across a large campus environment.Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously; effective verbal and written communication skills; proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.Experience with landscape design software (e.g., AutoCAD, GIS, SketchUp, Land F/X); knowledge of plant identification, tree care, turfgrass management, integrated pest management, irrigation systems, drainage principles, or landscape construction practices.Previous internship, work, or volunteer experience related to landscaping, grounds maintenance, parks, golf courses, athletic fields, arboriculture, nurseries, or horticulture.
